llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell and network use are expected for the disclosed publish and Drive helpers; the skill lists required binaries and credential sources, though a manifest-level permission declaration is absent.
[TP4] expected: Drive read, write, share-token, export, and delete functions are disclosed in the Drive section and script usage; they are high-impact but coherent with private cloud storage.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Some trigger phrases are ambiguous enough to cause accidental publishing if an agent does not ask follow-up questions; this is a scoping concern, not hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: Publishing to live URLs and public-link default access are disclosed, but users should still confirm intended visibility before upload.
[E1] expected: Uploading selected files to an API-returned upload URL is part of the expected upload flow; host validation would improve hardening, but the artifact does not show unrelated or deceptive exfiltration.
[E1] expected: Finalizing a publish is expected, but the script posts authorization headers to a server-returned finalize URL without validating its origin; this is a security-hardening issue rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[RA2] expected: Credential and claim-token persistence are explicitly documented for account continuity and anonymous site updates; users should remove these files when they no longer want the agent to retain access.
llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to publish selected local files to here.now or use here.now Drive storage. Before each publish, confirm whether the result should be public, password-protected, restricted, or private Drive-only. Treat ~/.herenow/credentials and .herenow/state.json as sensitive because they can preserve account access and claim tokens across sessions.
llm.summary: This is a disclosed publishing and private storage skill, but users should be careful because it can upload selected files, create public links, and persist account credentials.
